LESSON: SLAVERY AND SERVITUDE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and Relationships
Topic 2.3: Slavery and Servitude
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Slavery and Servitude, part of People, Population and Relationships in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: how in class while learners with Why has slavery and servitude existed for thousands of years?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Slavery and Servitude together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: Learners display team spirit as they work in groups to brainstorm on various forms of slavery and servitude

in traditional African society.

● Respect: Learners appreciates diverse opinions as they debate in class on various social injustices committed on the

Africans during Indian Ocean slave trade in 15th century.

● Responsibility: Learner cares for own property and those of others as they use print or digital resources to locate the

geographical extent of the regions covered by Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social cohesion: learners’ debate on the various social injustices committed on the Africans during Indian Ocean

slave trade in 15th century.

● Human Rights: Learner identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society and locate

areas where slaves were taken during Indian Ocean slave trade.

● Effective Communication: Learners debate various social injustices committed on the Africans during Indian

Ocean slave trade in 15th century.

18

Link to other learning Areas:

● English, Kiswahili and Kenyan Sign Language: Learners brainstorm on the forms of slavery and servitude.

Pre -Technical and Business Studies: Learner uses digital devices to research on the organisation of Indian Ocean slave

trade.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Digital resources with assistive technology, flip charts/manila papers, maps, approved textbooks, embossed/tactile

charts and embossed/tactile maps.
